To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MCC properties and the feed screw speed affect the roll compaction, and that the resulting ribbons, granules, and tablets have properties that are dependent on these design factors.
the properties of the roll compacted products can be predicted by the physical properties of the MCC, but also by the speed ratio.
the MCC properties bulk density, flowability, particle size, particle size distribution, compressibility, and friability influence the properties of the roll compacted ribbons, granules, and tablets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of orthogonal projections to latent spaces in experimental design to model the influence of MCC properties on roll compactor operation.
the influence of MCC physical properties on roll compactor performance, and the effect of roll compacted ribbons, granules, and tablets properties on the subsequent steps of tablet manufacturing.
the influence of the MCC properties on the roll compacted product properties and the subsequent tablet properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
roll compaction is a robust technique to produce tablets with good flowability and acceptable tensile strength.
the MCC properties and roll compactor speed ratio have a strong influence on the roll compactor performance, and consequently the quality of the ribbons, granules, and tablets.
roll compacted tablets with the highest tensile strength were produced using a low speed ratio and MCC with a high compressibility and a low bulk density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the roll compaction speed ratio is an important design factor for the tensile strengths of the granules and the tablets, while the MCC bulk density is the most important factor for the disintegration time of the tablets.
the MCC physical properties are the most important factors in roll compaction.
the roll compaction of different MCC grades resulted in ribbons with different porosity and granules with different porosity, bulk and tapped densities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physical characteristics of MCC are important in the roll compaction and granulation process.
orthogonal projections to latent spaces can be a useful tool in the development of roll compaction process.
the combination of factorial experimental design and orthogonal projection to latent structures provides a powerful tool to study the influence and interaction of several factors on a process.
